title: Dashboard version 2 and completed kidney testing in type 2 diabetes: a cohort across a staggered practice rollout
subtitle: Cohort study using a staggered rollout across 31 practices
statement: About 58 percent of 9,870 patients with type 2 diabetes in the network had both recommended kidney tests within 15 months, and the current dashboard is rarely opened. A redesigned dashboard with peer comparison, a target and a list of patients due reaches 16 practices in March 2026 and 15 in September 2026. The network needs to know whether the redesign increases completed testing, which features practices use, and whether it causes duplicate testing.
whoAffected: People with type 2 diabetes whose kidney disease may go undetected; practice recall clerks, nurses and managers; people tested in hospital clinics who may be recalled needlessly.
whatHurts: Missed early kidney disease and the treatment that could slow it, alongside wasted appointments and blood tests for people already tested elsewhere.
currentPractice: A dashboard of practice percentages with no patient list, peer comparison or target; recall is organised differently in each practice.
whyNow: The migration schedule creates six months in which half the practices have the new dashboard and half do not.
constraints: No budget beyond the implementation lead's time; practice system extracts and dashboard usage logs only; the migration schedule cannot be changed; no contact with patients.
patientCenteredGoal: People with diabetes have their kidneys checked when they are due, once, and act on the result.
summary: Problem framed as a cohort comparison across a staggered rollout, with completed tests as the outcome.
